title: Online Mindfulness-based Dance/Movement Therapy on Physical Activity and Whole-Person Health in Older Adults
official: Evaluating the Effects of Online Group Mindfulness-based Dance/Movement Therapy on Physical Activity and Whole-Person Health in Older Adults
summary: This randomized controlled trial will examine whether an online, group-based Mindfulness-based Dance/Movement Therapy (M-DMT) intervention can increase physical activity and improve whole-person health among sedentary older adults. M-DMT combines mindful movement, creative expression, and interpersonal connection to support physical, cognitive, emotional, and social well-being. Participants will be randomly assigned to either M-DMT or the Stony Brook Health Education Program (HEP). The study will evaluate changes in physical activity, measured through self-report and accelerometry, as well as multiple dimensions of whole-person health. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, immediately following the 12-week intervention, and at a 3-month follow-up. Qualitative interviews will further explore participants' experiences with the interventions and their perceived effects on health and daily life.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 65-85 years.
* Insufficiently physically active, defined as engaging in less than 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity physical activity or less than 75 minutes per week of vigorous-intensity physical activity, as assessed during screening.
* Able to use a computer, tablet, or smartphone to participate in online intervention sessions and complete study assessments, with or without assistance.
* Have adequate vision and hearing, with or without correction, to safely participate in online group sessions and complete study procedures.
* Able to safely engage in mild-to-moderate physical activity, as determined through a virtual physical safety screening conducted by a physical therapist or trained study personnel.
* Have sufficient cognitive capacity to provide informed consent and participate in study procedures, as assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Telehealth Version (MoCA-T). Individuals scoring 26 or higher will be considered eligible based on cognitive screening.
* Able and willing to provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Significant cognitive impairment, defined as a MoCA-T score below 18, or cognitive difficulties that prevent informed consent or safe participation.
* Use of mobility aids, including a cane, walker, or wheelchair, or physical limitations that would prevent safe participation in movement-based activities.
* Medical conditions that contraindicate participation in mild-to-moderate physical activity, as determined during the physical safety screening.
* Surgery within the previous six months that may limit safe participation in physical activity.
* Physician recommendations or restrictions against participation in moderate physical activity or exercise.
* A recently diagnosed serious mental health condition that may interfere with participation in study procedures.
* Any additional medical, physical, cognitive, or safety concern that, in the judgment of the study investigators, would make participation unsafe or compromise the integrity of the study.
